front: Where is the IVC measured for RA pressure estimation?
back: Subcostal view, ~1–2 cm from the RA-IVC junction (before the hepatic vein confluence), at end-expiration or during average tidal breathing.

front: IVC parameters for a NORMAL RA pressure of ~3 mmHg?
back: IVC diameter ≤ 2.1 cm AND > 50% collapse with sniff.

front: IVC parameters for an ELEVATED RA pressure of ~15 mmHg?
back: IVC diameter > 2.1 cm AND < 50% collapse with sniff.

front: When is IVC-based RA pressure estimation unreliable?
back: Mechanically ventilated patients (positive-pressure ventilation reverses normal respiratory dynamics) and highly trained athletes (baseline vena caval dilation).

front: IVC plethora and RA inversion — sensitivity/specificity for tamponade?
back: IVC plethora is SENSITIVE (present in nearly all significant tamponade). RA inversion > 1/3 of the cardiac cycle is more sensitive but less specific than RV diastolic collapse, which is highly SPECIFIC for tamponade.

front: Describe azygous continuation of an interrupted IVC.
back: Congenital absence of the intrahepatic IVC — venous return continues through a dilated azygous vein (posterior to the aorta) to the SVC. Associated with polysplenia (left isomerism / heterotaxy).

front: Where does a persistent left SVC drain and how is it diagnosed on echo?
back: Drains into the coronary sinus → produces a dilated CS. Diagnosed by injecting agitated saline into the LEFT arm — bubbles appear in the CS before the RA.
